name: capacity-drill
scope: One container of the pinned database image (public.ecr.aws/supabase/postgres:17.6.1.166) on the workstation, with the database tier's limits where stated (1024 MiB memory and swap; CPUs and process limit as listed; runs without a process limit listed had Docker's default, no limit). N databases, each initialised with pgbench scale 5, then all loaded at once with pgbench's default read and write transaction for the stated seconds, each with the stated number of client connections (18 is an environment's base connection limit: Auth 6, REST 6, Storage 6). Peak memory is the highest docker stats sample, taken every two seconds. No Auth, REST, Storage, Realtime or gateway process ran; no logical decoding, no PostgREST schema cache, no application queries. It measures the shared database under connection load, not a whole installation and not real traffic.
script: lab/capacity-drill.sh (committed after the runs, from the script that produced them): docker run with --memory, --cpus and --pids-limit, CREATE DATABASE, pgbench -i -s 5, then pgbench -c CLIENTS -j 2 -T SECONDS -n per database in parallel.

runs.note: The tier's process limit of the time: six of the eight pgbench runs failed to open their connections (one process per connection).

alter_system: In the same image, ALTER SYSTEM SET max_connections = 200 as supabase_admin, then docker restart of the same container: max_connections read 200, source configuration file /var/lib/postgresql/data/postgresql.auto.conf.
server_shape: The real server has 4 cores and 16 GiB. Placement admits CPU ceilings up to twice the cores after one is kept for the host (6), and 1.75 CPUs for an empty installation plus 0.5 per environment: eight environments without Realtime or Edge Functions.
conclusion: Eight environments at their base connection limit, and 192 busy connections in all, fit the 1 GiB, one CPU database tier with a process limit of 320 (peak 613 MiB); at the earlier limit of 128 processes the connections could not be opened. Latency with every client running at once rose from about 86 ms (4 environments) to about 100 to 136 ms (8). These are allocation limits checked by a synthetic drill, not measured capacity for real traffic.
pids_update: docker update --pids-limit 320 on a running container of the pinned image changed HostConfig.PidsLimit from 128 to 320 with the same container id and start time, without a restart.
